It was a meeting to which they had invited -- it was a large meeting, and there were high-ranking commanders and lower ranking commanders, and even the commanders of the civilian defence which existed at the time, and all those people. So that it wasn't a meeting of a close type -- it wasn't of that type, although it wasn't quite an open-ended meeting. One could enter it. Since I was very close to Anto Pejcinovic all the time, I do not think that my presence there bothered anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But who invited you to that meeting, and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, I am just -- I just told you. It wasn't a closed meeting, because all the commanders were there: lower commanders, higher commanders, senior commanders, and members. And we, HOS members, who were there and could go there to hear what was going on, what was happening in Vares, what was -- and also hear what was going on outside Vares. So it wasn't a meeting with special invitation cards; it was simply an open meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you saw that, all that you mentioned, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Pejcinovic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And how did this order reach Vares? By what route?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: With a convoy, because convoy -- Caritas convoy was coming in, and I think that -- I don't think; I affirm that fuel also came with the convoy, about two or three fuel assistants with the convoy. And that is how it reached Vares. And I believe that Vjeran Mijatovic was one of those who escorted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And who issued that document? What did it say? What was the heading? What did it say?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, it was an A4 format, and in one corner it had the coat of arms of the HVO, with the chequerboard, and at the bottom it was short. I saw it only because Anto Pejcinovic had it on the desk, had it on the table beforehand. But Zvonko Duznovic picked it up and said, "We are strong enough. We don't need any help." And he took it very boldly, read it, and put it away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let's go back to the document. Who was the document addressed to?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, the HVO in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: There was no name specified on it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, everybody knows who was the head, because Anto Pejcinovic was both the political and military leader of Vares. His was to say who would be the commander in the municipality, who would be at the checkpoint, at the fuel -- at the petrol station, so on and so forth. So when I said beforehand that on paper there were various leaders, but everybody knew who had the upper say; it was the president of the HDZ. And the HDZ president was also at the same time the president of the Croatian Defence Council, except that the commander for a time was Boro Mamisic. So the letter was addressed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that document which came with the convoy, it was the original letter, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: You mean original?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I mean, it was not a copy; it was an original.

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, they all looked the same. They are official letters. Whether that was a copy or --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But since we are talking about the document and describing it, apart from that sentence that they could turn to Serbs for the assistance for the defence of Vares, was there something else in the document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Why, yes. This was read out. But I really couldn't remember it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It was one and the same document. It was a long document or not?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, no, it wasn't a very long document, but it was a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So other subjects were broached, apart from the one that you didn't memorise?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, it was concise and there was so many lines. There was so many lines in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But whose signature was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, I did not have this document in my hands. Had I had it in my hands, I would have remembered. But it said in one of the corners there was -- it said "sent to," and there were three lines and the signature. But I do not know whether it was the official label and whether it had typed "Mate Boban" or "Dario Kordic" or something else. I do not know. But I think that there were two names mentioned, because it said "for" somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was there Mate Boban's name there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: I believe that Mate Boban's name was typed, but it could have been initialled by Dario Kordic, or the other way around. Perhaps Mate Boban's name was typed down in the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, there was no Dario Kordic's name typed?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: No, his name was not typed, but I think that the signature was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was there a signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever -- did you ever see Mr. Kordic's signature before that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you're saying that this was Dario Kordic's signature?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Yes, I think, in all likelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you are not sure? You are not positive whether somebody else has put his name or whether it was in his own writing?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. It was his signature, but whether he signed it in his own hand or whether somebody else signed it in his name, that -- but that was just initialled, it was only initialled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we're referring to a document which arrived in September '93, and will you agree with me that Busovaca, as of April '93, was completely cut off and surrounded by the BH army's troops from all sides, cut off from both Vares and Grude?

utterances.speaker: Witness AO
utterances.text: Do I agree that Busovaca was cut off from all the municipalities? Yes, well, I agree. Well, I don't know 100 per cent, but I do think it was cut off. But I also say that Vares was also cut off from all Croat places, and yet Vares had its command --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no need to go on. Now, Mr. Naumovski, it's half past 5. How much longer are you going to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure I can finish by 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you must finish within half an hour tomorrow morning. Will you tailor your cross-examination? You will then have had the best part of two hours to cross-examine. But I think we've had enough for one day. Witness AO, I'm afraid we can't finish your evidence today. Could you be back tomorrow morning, please, at 9, when we will conclude it, and you'll then be released. But will you be back, please, at 9. We'll adjourn now until 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The order of witnesses tomorrow has to be slightly different, because one witness has to get out. I'll notify your staff accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
